Prior predictive check

Source: R/prediction.R
prior_predictive_check.Rd

Fits the model using only the priors (ignoring the observed events) and plots the data the model would predict. This shows whether the priors imply plausible data before any data are seen. A prior describes which values of a parameter are plausible before seeing the data. Use it before fitting with bison_model(): if the predicted rates are implausible for the species and sampling method, change the priors.

Usage

prior_predictive_check(
  formula,
  data,
  model_type,
  plot_type = "density",
  options = NULL,
  priors = NULL,
  directed = isTRUE(options$directed),
  num_draws = 50,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula, data, model_type, priors

As for bison_model(). The data are used for the structure of the model (dyads and observation effort), not for the events.

plot_type

Type of predictive plot, passed to plot_predictions() as type: "density" or "stats".

options

A list of extra options. Currently only directed (TRUE/FALSE) is used; prefer the directed argument.

directed

Whether the network is directed.

num_draws

Number of datasets to simulate from the priors.

...

Further arguments passed to bison_model().

Value

The prior-only model, invisibly.

See also

prior_check() to plot the priors themselves, get_default_priors(), plot_predictions()

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = TRUE)
prior_predictive_check(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim,
  model_type = "binary_conjugate",
  priors = get_default_priors("binary_conjugate")
)
